title: One Small Kindness
subtitle: Speaking to yourself as you would to a friend
summary: Self-kindness is a habit of tone more than a feeling. This lesson looks at the voice we use with ourselves and offers one gentle way to soften it.

teaching.text: Listen for a moment to the voice that comments on your day. For many people it is quick, certain and a little sharp. It notices what went wrong before what went well. It would not be welcome at a friend's table, yet it sits at ours every evening.
Self-kindness does not ask you to believe anything untrue about yourself. It asks only for a change of tone: the tone you would use with someone you cared about who had the same hard day you did.

items: Kindness is not the same as letting yourself off. You can be honest and gentle at once.
Kindness is not a mood you wait for. It is a sentence you choose.
Kindness gets easier with repetition, like any other habit of speech.

teaching.text: Research on self-compassion suggests that people who treat themselves with warmth after setbacks tend to recover and try again more readily than people who rely on harsh self-criticism. Warmth, it turns out, is not soft on results.

blocks.text: Write one sentence to yourself in the journal, in the voice you would use for a good friend. It can be as plain as: "Today was a lot, and you got through it."
One sentence is enough. You do not have to mean it fully yet.

reflectionQuestions: What did the voice in your head say about you today? Was it fair?
Who in your life speaks to you kindly? What do they sound like?
What would change if you borrowed that tone for one evening?
encouragement: A kinder tone is not something you earn. It is something you can start using now, clumsily, and that is fine.
